title: Supreme Court: APTEL Cannot Use Its Review Power to Overturn a Settled Supreme Court Ruling
case_name: Damodar Valley Corporation v. Maithan Alloys Limited and Others
citation: 2026 INSC 1178; Civil Appeal No. 11106 of 2024, decided 30 October 2026
card_summary: The Supreme Court set aside an APTEL review order that had reversed the tribunal's own 2019 decision letting Damodar Valley Corporation recover its sinking fund contribution through tariff alongside depreciation. The Court held its 2018 ruling in Bhaskar Shrachi Alloys had already settled the point, so a tribunal's review power cannot be used to override a binding Supreme Court judgment.
card_tip: Once the Supreme Court has settled a tariff question, treat a tribunal's review of its own earlier order on the same point as vulnerable, however many years have passed since the original decision.
verification_notes: Confirmed via SupremeToday.ai's case report and a copy of the judgment PDF hosted on Verdictum, consistent with Courtbook's summary of the costs order. Reported cost figure (Rs 35 lakh, per Courtbook headline) not independently cross-checked against the judgment text and is omitted from the card for that reason.
